answer: Staked deposits slashed on rejection work like this: an agent must post collateral to register an identity, and if its work is rejected as invalid, that stake is forfeited. Faking identities becomes costly, since each sybil burns real capital. It is an oasis of accountability in a desert of anonymous agents, and every slashed deposit cuts one thread of a would-be sybil swarm before it can form a reef of fake consensus. What it does not solve: collusion among genuinely funded agents, stake borrowed from the same controller, or rejection errors that punish honest agents. It raises the.
